workload: PELT change-point detection (L2 cost) on a length-2000 piecewise-constant signal with five segments. Baseline is ruptures.Pelt(model=l2, jump=1), the exact reference the equivalence suite checks against; both find the same breakpoints [400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2000]. Throughput is samples/sec (signal length processed per second).

methodology.aggregation: median of repeated timed runs, warm-up excluded

gate.note: PELT is an inherently sequential O(n^2) dynamic program (at jump=1) that ruptures implements in pure Python; neither library vectorizes it, so the interpreted loop pays full per-step overhead. jump=1 is the apples-to-apples setting that matches the Rust exact DP and the equivalence-suite breakpoints; ruptures' default jump=5 is ~25x faster but skips candidate positions and is a different (approximate) algorithm. The gate uses the exact-equivalent jump=1 comparison.

latency.note: Per-sample processing cost ~3.3 ns derived from the 300 Ksample/s rate, warm-up excluded; far under the sub-millisecond budget. (A full 2000-sample PELT run takes ~6.7 ms end to end.)

out_of_scope.algorithms: batch clustering / decomposition / change-point detection over a full dataset, not streaming estimators (no online formulation)

known_debt: Only PELT change-point is benched as the family's gated hot path; the clustering (k-means, DBSCAN, ...) and decomposition (PCA, ICA, ...) algorithms are not separately gated. Some of those compare against vectorized sklearn and would not necessarily clear 2.0x on dense linear-algebra-bound steps.
